audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly asserts that Malzahar has "no shield", "no way to escape or interrupt", "zero mobility or defensive tools" and "no counterplay available to him". Void Shift gives him massive damage reduction AND crowd control immunity whenever he has not recently taken damage — which means a stocked Pyromania thrown at an untouched Malzahar is ignored outright. That is the single most important fact in this matchup and the content layer denies it in six separate fields.
audit.why: Riot's passive text is unambiguous. The full layer already knew this (tldr: "His shield eats your stun and ruins the whole combo") — the two layers were telling a paying user opposite things about whether her stun works. Correct play is Q or auto first to strip Void Shift, then spend the glow.
audit.corrected: whys[0], whys[2], whys[5], early, mid, late, spikes[1].text and spikes[2].text all rewritten around stripping Void Shift first; tradeGood/tradeBad/breakdown.trading/breakdown.carry rebuilt on the same sequence.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Malzahar/Skill/Skill; content win[] and the packet both read Annie on rows 0-5 and Malzahar at 2+ items. Six of seven rows disagree, and the two layers name opposite winners at Level 6.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140 seconds at rank 1 — Annie's Tibbers is 130 — so level 6 does not belong to Malzahar; his ult is a once-a-lane-phase button early. It becomes his at two items when it drops to 80s and a tank peels for him. That ordering matches both the packet and 51.15% over 1130 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid claimed "Level 6 changes nothing for him defensively; Malefic Visions is a DoT, not a fight-winning tool" — it treats Malefic Visions (his E) as the level 6 event and ignores Nether Grasp entirely.
audit.why: Level 6 gives him a 700-range point-and-click suppression. It is not fight-winning at 140 seconds, but describing his level 6 as a damage-over-time is wrong in a way that gets a player killed walking up at 6.
audit.corrected: mid, whys[4] and spikes[1].text now name Nether Grasp and give its cooldown as the thing to track.

audit.whatIsWrong: The `early` paragraph refers to "Null Zone" — an ability that does not exist in Malzahar's kit. packet.suspectNames was empty, so no automated check caught it.
audit.why: His R is Nether Grasp; there is no Null Zone. This is exactly the class of fabricated name the calibration list warns about, and it survived because the name-checker found no near-miss.
audit.corrected: Rewritten out of the early paragraph, which now names Void Swarm (150 range) and Call of the Void instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d described Nether Grasp as a "fifteen-second" invitation. It is 140/110/80.
audit.why: Off by an order of magnitude on the cooldown the page tells you to count. A spent Nether Grasp at rank 1 is a two-minute window, not fifteen seconds — the correction makes the advice far more aggressive, correctly.
audit.corrected: Now a 140-second invitation; breakdown.cooldowns carries the full 140-to-80 progression plus the note that Void Shift has no readable timer at all.

edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours, but not for free: Void Shift gives him massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity until he takes damage, so a stocked stun thrown into an untouched Malzahar is simply ignored. edits.before: This snowballs through levels 3-6 as Malzahar simply has no engage or escape — every all-in you commit to lands cleanly since he can't reposition or interrupt your combo. edits.after: This holds through levels 3-5: Malzahar has no dash and no escape, so every all-in you commit to lands — provided you have already stripped Void Shift, because an untouched Malzahar shrugs the stun off entirely. Level 6 does change things: Nether Grasp is a point-and-click suppression that no cleanse in your kit answers, but it is 140 seconds at rank 1, so track that timer and fight in the gap. Keep pushing him under tower whenever it is down.

edits.before: Your first item spike lets you outright delete Malzahar in a single rotation if he's ever caught missing Zhonya's — he has no shield, no dash, no way to survive burst. His only real save is Nether Grasp lockdown in 5v5s once he's got a support/tank peeling for him and enough AP for his ult to matter, so play around vision and don't get isolated late even though you dominate every 1v1.
edits.after: Your first item deletes Malzahar in a single rotation, but only into a Void Shift that is already broken — open with a Q or an auto, never with the stun, or the whole combo is wasted on damage reduction and CC immunity. His win condition is Nether Grasp in 5v5s once a tank peels for him: 140 seconds at rank 1, so late fights start when you have seen it spent, and you never walk a side lane alone when you have not.
